issue.title: fix(ci+docs): repair the silent-except gate that never ran, and the API docs nobody could use
issue.body:
Audit + workflow-completion pass over `main` (71f83625). 20 commits, in an isolated worktree so it never touched the other agent's tree.

**Standing rule: no finding is actioned until it is reproduced on the current tree.** Both supplied audits were written against *other* commits and contained many claims that were already fixed or never true. Two of my own fixes in this branch were also caught being wrong by the guards I added. Evidence table: [`docs/audit/CLAIMS-VERIFIED.md`](docs/audit/CLAIMS-VERIFIED.md).

## The product bugs (what actually mattered)

**The Charm tab never had data.** `SkylitHeatmapGrid` maps Charm → `grid.charm_grid`, but only the local Black-Scholes path emitted it. The *vendor-greek* path — what actually serves the app — returned no `charm_grid`, so selecting Charm always rendered "surface unavailable in this snapshot" on a healthy payload. Added `compute_charm_grid_local` mirroring the VEX surface, wired into `server.py` with its own status. Missing coverage reports `PARTIAL_CHARM_COVERAGE`; an absent Greek is never zero-filled.

**The WallInspector "VEX gross / net" row was permanently "—".** It read `grids.grid.vex_grid`, but `metrics.grids` is a *map of named overlays* (`{raw, delta, activity, vendor}`), so `grids.grid` was always undefined. VEX lives on the payload's own `grid.vex_grid`. The existing test fixture had encoded the *same mistake*, which is why it passed while broken — fixture corrected.

**Triad had three permanently-blank columns and a wrong-expiry bug.** IV, Delta and per-row expiry don't exist on the `/api/data` heatmap payload (its strike rows carry exactly 27 aggregate keys — verified by calling the route). So the trade panel opened with no IV/delta, and `row.expiry || expiries[0]` requested the *wrong* contract expiry. Real IV/delta/expiry live on `/api/chain/{ticker}`. Repointed at fields that exist, and fixed a stale `useCallback` dep this exposed.

**`CLAUDE.md` claimed `OrderRouter` "has no callers"** — so that its default-deny MARKET gate "protects nothing". False: `discord_bot.py` builds it, making it the only paper-order path. A doc saying a live gate protects nothing is exactly what gets someone to weaken it.

**Schwab removed entirely** (retired 2026-09-03, deleted 2026-09-27): two services, six test modules, two Grafana panels that charted dead metrics, and a runbook telling operators to restart a streamer that no longer exists. `mock_schwab_feed` → `mock_synthetic_feed` (it was never a broker connection — a GBM generator behind a dev flag). Guards now fail if it returns.

## CI/infra that never ran

- The **silent-except gate had never once executed** — `working-directory: backend` with the script at repo root, exit 2 on every push.
- **Observability stack mounted the wrong directory** (6 binds → the repo's *parent*), so Prometheus and Grafana came up with no config and no dashboards, reporting healthy.
- Grafana fought the dev frontend for `:3000`; prod Prometheus had no `extra_hosts` and was never scraping.
- API reference had an **empty Path cell in all 159 rows**; spec held 156 paths against 369 real routes.
- `CLAUDE.md` told you to run a nonexistent Windows venv and **forbade the one that works**.
- The secret-scan gate was scanning a **different repository**.

## Gates

| | |
|---|---|
| Backend | **13 failed / 5429 passed** — failure list **byte-identical** to the pre-change baseline |
| Frontend | **72/72 suites, 619/619 tests**; production build compiles |
| Lint | ruff clean across the backend |

Every new test was verified to **fail against the original broken code** before being trusted. Two intermediate regressions were caught by existing tests during this work, which is the point of having them.

## Two things I did not do

- **Secret rotation** for anything ever committed (`db-PBRQ…` in git history). Rotate at the provider, *then* purge. History rewrites need explicit authorization.
- **Did not delete the unverified dead-code list.** Spot-checks found it wrong (13 dead frontend modules, not 17; a "shadowed route" that was never shadowed).

## The 13 red tests

Pre-existing on `main` since 2026-09-04. **Hermes fixed them on `feat/node-confluence-overlay` (PR #56, `f0fe42d4`) but that branch is not merged**, so they are not in `main`. This branch does not touch any of those files.

No merge without authorization.

issue.title: docs(audit): record unverified artifacts the CI truth audit does not surface
issue.body:
## What

`qc/audit/truth_audit.sh` runs as step 4 of every CI `backend-tests` job and is
the repo's only automated overfit check. Its model rules (9-12) only **block**
when the commit subject claims ML work; on anything else they print `WARN`.
That scoping is deliberate — the script's comments say enforcing
unconditionally "would block unrelated work on pre-existing model debt — the
fastest way to get a gate switched off."

So normal commits report `24 passed, 0 failed` while the debt is unread.

## The finding

Reproduced on `origin/main` with an empty commit that trips the trigger
(`git commit --allow-empty -m 'chore: quarantine degenerate models'`):

**6 violations across 24 audited models.** All live under `backend/models/`,
none quarantined, all trained 2026-05-24.

| Model | Finding |
|---|---|
| `SPY_rf_20260524_020801` | **`avg_test_sharpe` 8.0202** (threshold 5), accuracy 0.82 |
| `SPY_rf_20260524_020801` | ratio **0.28125** — 45 features / 160 samples |
| `IWM_rf_20260524_022147` | ratio 0.275 — 44 / 160 |
| `TLT_rf_20260524_022154` | ratio 0.275 — 44 / 160 |
| `QQQ_rf_20260524_022055` | ratio 0.275 — 44 / 160 |
| `QQQ_rf_20260524_022118` | ratio 0.275 — 44 / 160 |

Every figure was re-read from the JSON directly, not taken from the audit's own
output — a gate reporting its own findings is not independent verification.

## What this is not

A measurement, not a verdict. Nothing is retrained or quarantined here. Four
tickers failing the identical ratio at the identical sample count points at one
shared training configuration, not four independent problems, and whether 44
features on 160 samples is acceptable is a modeling decision.

The Sharpe 8.02 is the one to look at first: above 5 on *daily direction* is
the exact signature Rule 9 exists to catch.

**This is not evidence of predictive skill.** An overfit artifact is evidence
about the fitting procedure, not about the market. Docs only.

issue.title: fix(qc): audit the *_manifest.json descriptors the truth audit was blind to
issue.body:
## The gap

`qc/audit/truth_audit.sh` runs as step 4 of every CI `backend-tests` job and is
the repo's only automated overfit check. Its discovery:

    find models backend/models -maxdepth 2 -type f \
        \( -name '*_meta_*.json' -o -name '*_meta.json' -o -name 'meta_*.json' \)

matches three patterns and finds **8** descriptors. This repo also uses
`*_manifest.json` — matched by none of them. Adding it finds **84**.

So 76 descriptors were invisible to rules 9-12, including all 11 live
root-tree manifests.

## What it was hiding

`models/SPY_gbm_production_manifest.json`:

    n_features 53, n_samples 167  ->  ratio 0.3174  (threshold 0.2)  VIOLATION

This is the one that matters. It is production-named, and it lives in the
directory the live loader actually reads — `ml_price_prediction.py:210-218`
resolves repo-root `models/`. Its own `gate_results` record only
`class_balance`, `feature_variance`, `prediction_distribution`: no Sharpe
ceiling, no sample floor, no ratio. The overfit guards were never run against it.

It also violates the ratio rule more severely than any of the six descriptors
the gate *did* inspect (0.3174 vs 0.28125) — those six are in
`backend/models/`, which no code path globs.

## Proof

Measured in a throwaway worktree, before and after:

    before:  grep -c SPY_gbm_production_manifest  ->  0        (blind to it)
    after:   ratio 0.31736526946107785 > 0.2 (53 features / 167 samples)  FAIL

## Enforcement scoping is unchanged

The existing WARN/FAIL split still holds, and is what makes this safe:

| Commit subject | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| does not claim ML work | 24 passed, 0 failed | **226 passed, 0 failed** (new findings print WARN) |
| claims ML/model work | 6 findings, FAIL | **7 findings, FAIL** |

Unrelated work is not blocked; a commit that actually touches these artifacts
now fails on a violation it previously could not see.

No change was needed to the metric extractor — `n_samples` and `n_features` are
top-level in this schema and `first()` already handles them without
`fold_details`. **Absent stays `NA`:** `SPY_gbm_production` records no sharpe,
and the gate correctly prints `SKIP / NOT verified` rather than scoring it.

## Scope

No model is retrained, quarantined, or deleted. This changes what the gate can
see, nothing about the models themselves. Whether 53 features on 167 samples is
acceptable remains a separate judgment call, recorded in #60.

issue.title: test(qc): self-test for the truth-audit gate widened in #61
issue.body:
## Why

`qc/audit/truth_audit.sh` runs as step 4 of every CI `backend-tests` job and is
the repo's only automated overfit check. Its silent-except sibling has 27
tests. This one had **none** — which is how it went on inspecting 8 of 84 model
descriptors while reporting `PASS`, until #61 widened the `find`.

A gate with no test of its own is one rename away from silently covering less,
and it will not tell you.

## What is covered

21 tests, all over `tmp_path` fixtures. None read the live model tree, so only
changing the gate's own behaviour can break them.

- **Discovery** — each of the four filename conventions must still match
  something, and five real descriptors must stay reachable. This is the direct
  guard on the #61 regression.
- **The four metric verdicts** — ratio ceiling, Sharpe ceiling, healthy pass,
  and `absent` → `SKIP`.
- **The WARN/FAIL split** — a ratio violation must WARN and exit 0 on a docs
  commit; a clean docs commit must pass. A gate that blocks unrelated work gets
  switched off, which is worse than one that under-reports.
- **Subject-line scoping** — `model` in a commit *body* must not trip the ML
  rules.

## Two of my own assertions were wrong

Both caught by running the gate rather than reasoning about it:

1. A fixture with `sharpe` under `metrics.sharpe` scored `SKIP`. The extractor
   reads Sharpe from the document root only, and the real
   `SPY_gbm_production_manifest.json` records no Sharpe anywhere — its `metrics`
   block holds train/test accuracy, precision, recall, f1, `train_samples`. My
   fixture had invented a schema the gate does not read; `SKIP` was correct.
2. A docs commit over an empty model tree "should" pass. It must **not**: the
   gate fails when it inspects zero descriptors, which is right — a `find`
   matching nothing is exactly the shape #61 had.

## Mutation-verified

Reverting the #61 `find` pattern in a scratch worktree turns **8 of these red**,
including `test_manifest_fixtures_are_inspected`, the direct guard on the
discovery regression.

    with fix:     21 passed
    fix reverted:  8 failed, 13 passed

Test-only. No gate or model behaviour changed.

issue.title: fix(agent,compose,api): unblock CI on three independent failures
issue.body:
Fixes two independent CI failures, both reproduced rather than inferred.

## 1. `fix(agent)` — unjustified silent except

```
backend/services/agent/model.py:214: pass    [unjustified]
1 unjustified silent handler site(s) across 326 scanned file(s).
```

A 6-line justification comment. No behaviour change — the production diff is
6 insertions, 0 deletions.

Before writing the comment I checked whether the swallow was actually
*correct*, because a justification that misstates the reason is worse than
none. It is correct, and specifically so:

- a failed settlement must not fail the request;
- `accounted` stays `False`, so the result reports `accounting="reserved"` and
  `actual_cost=None` rather than claiming the generation was billed;
- `reconcile()` looks the generation up by id via `GET /generation`, which
  never repeats the paid request.

The two neighbouring handlers already use `contextlib.suppress`, which reads as
self-documenting. This one used `try/except: pass`, so the intent was invisible.

Nothing pinned the behaviour — the swallow could have become "report settled
anyway" and no test would have noticed. `tests/agent/test_settlement_failure_path.py`
covers both halves of the split.

**Mutation-verified:** reverting the swallow to claim success
(`accounted = True` in the handler) fails
`test_failed_settlement_reports_reserved_and_never_claims_billed`. That is the
exact regression that would tell the ledger a generation was billed when the
reservation was never consumed.

## 2. `docs(api)` — 13 undocumented routes

The "API docs match the app" step also failed. It is **not** caused by the
settlement change: it reproduces on clean `origin/main`, so it is a
pre-existing failure the earlier integration left behind.

13 routes are live in the app but missing from the committed snapshot
(357 → 370 paths), including several this repo's own audit work added or
verified live earlier — `node-confluence` and the `universe` scan/leaderboard
routes:

```
/api/agent/{history,models,session,session/logout,session/recover,session/rotate}
/api/flowseeker/{market-session,universe/leaderboard,universe/scan}
/api/heatseeker/{node-confluence,price-history/{ticker}}
/api/market/{catalog,provider-updates}
```

Checked rather than assumed:

- `generate_api_docs.py --check` now exits 0: `API docs up to date (370 paths)`
- **0 new order-placement routes.** The `/api/alpaca/order*` paths present in
  the snapshot pre-date this change and were already documented, so
  regenerating does not widen the data router's surface.
- **0 paths removed.** Every previously documented route survives.

## Evidence

- `tests/agent/`: 410 passed (408 before, 2 added)
- `tests/test_compose_consistency.py`: 31 passed
- `ruff`: clean
- `check_silent_excepts.py`: OK, 326 files
- `truth_audit.sh`: 228 passed, 0 failed

### A local failure that is not a code defect

`test_schwab_is_fully_removed_from_the_tree` failed locally with
`retired Schwab artifacts are back: ['backend/tests/schwab']`. That directory
held only gitignored `__pycache__/*.pyc` leftovers from an earlier session and
zero tracked files, so removing it cleared the local run.

Verified it does not affect CI: on a pristine checkout of this branch the test
fails for an unrelated reason (`bind-mount sources that do not exist:
frontend/build`), and passes 31/31 once `frontend/build` exists — which CI's
frontend job produces before the backend job runs.

## Note

issue.title: docs: restore the CLAUDE.md venv fix that a side-branch recovery reverted
issue.body:
`test_version_doc_consistency::test_claude_md_does_not_point_at_a_nonexistent_windows_venv`
fails on main. **The test is correct — the doc had regressed.**

## What happened

`abb8c488` ("CLAUDE.md pointed at a venv that does not exist and forbade the one
that works") fixed this deliberately and added the test. Its message states
plainly that *there is no `.venv313` directory* and that the Windows
`Scripts/*.exe` form is wrong for a POSIX repo.

Then `a590d0e3` — "Recover useful side-branch work with verified reconciliation
evidence" — reintroduced all 12 `.venv313` lines. `abb8c488` is an **ancestor** of
`a590d0e3`, so the side-branch recovery overwrote a fix that was already merged.

## The misdiagnosis I nearly shipped

This looked identical to the compose bind-mount bug fixed in #63 — an assertion
about a path that only exists on one machine. I wrote a `sys.platform == "win32"`
guard to scope the check to Windows, and it passed locally.

Then I read the original commit message. The author considered the path wrong on
**every** platform, not just non-Windows. So the guard would have silenced a
correct check to make a red test go green — the wrong fix for a real doc bug.
That patch is reverted and is **not** in this commit.

## What changed, each verified against this checkout

- **8 runnable commands** pointed at `.venv313/Scripts/python.exe` now use
  `cd backend && .venv/bin/python`. Confirmed working: `--collect-only`
  collects 6410 tests; `uvicorn` imports.
- **The ruff line claimed the venv provides ruff. It does not** —
  `python -m ruff` returns `No module named ruff`. Ruff is a standalone binary
  at `/opt/homebrew/bin/ruff` (0.15.22). The doc now says that.
- **The Dev Environment claimed the venv is Python 3.12. It is 3.14.6** — newer
  than the 3.12 ship pin, so it can accept syntax the image would not. The doc
  now warns about that and points at `ruff` `target-version` and
  `requires-python` as the authority.
- **The "Windows environments" block claimed `backend/.venv/bin/python` does not
  exist and told readers to avoid it.** That is the exact inverse of reality
  and was the most harmful line in the file. Replaced with verified local facts.

The one surviving `.venv313` mention is prose stating the directory is *absent*,
which the test permits by design — its docstring says it checks command lines
only, so prose explaining the old path was wrong does not trip the gate.

## Evidence

- `test_version_doc_consistency.py`: 5 passed
- 90 passed across version-doc + compose + truth-audit + silent-except suites
- `truth_audit.sh`: passed, 0 failed

Docs only — 1 file, no code, no test, no config.

issue.title: chore(gitignore): cover the SQLite runtime stores the duckdb rules missed
issue.body:
Running the backend left three untracked files in `backend/data/`:

```
backend/data/scan_observations.sqlite3
backend/data/scan_observations.sqlite3-wal
backend/data/scan_observations.sqlite3-shm
```

A dirty tree from merely starting the server is how runtime state ends up
committed by accident, and it masks real changes in `git status`.

## The existing rules were half-dead

`.gitignore` had `data/*.duckdb` and `data/*.duckdb.wal`. A pattern containing a
slash is **anchored to the directory holding the .gitignore**, so `data/*.duckdb`
only ever matched the **repo-root** `data/`. It never reached `backend/data/` at
all — and the sqlite store that appeared there was covered by no rule whatsoever.

## Verified with `git check-ignore` on each real path

| path | after |
|---|---|
| `data/journal.duckdb` | IGNORED |
| `data/journal.duckdb.wal` | IGNORED |
| `backend/data/scan_observations.sqlite3` | IGNORED |
| `backend/data/scan_observations.sqlite3-wal` | IGNORED |
| `backend/data/scan_observations.sqlite3-shm` | IGNORED |

## Two stores deliberately NOT matched

```
data/research_kg.duckdb        (23 MB, tracked)
backend/data/gflows.duckdb     (1 MB, tracked)
```

Both are **committed** to the repo, and ignoring a tracked file does nothing
anyway. Whether they belong in git is a separate question this PR does not
touch — adding patterns for them would be misleading, since it would suggest
they are ignored when they are in fact tracked.

The repo-root patterns are kept alongside the new `backend/` ones because **both**
`data/` directories are real and both hold runtime state. My first pass concluded
the root `data/` did not exist and removed the old rules; a directory listing
showed otherwise, so the old rules are preserved and extended.

1 file, `.gitignore` only.

issue.title: fix(requirements,test): make @pytest.mark.flaky functional and seed the test that flaked
issue.body:
Two related defects, found by an actual failure rather than by inspection.

## 1. `@pytest.mark.flaky` was inert on 8 tests

`backend/pytest.ini` registers a `flaky` marker and 8 tests use it, but
`pytest-rerunfailures` was in no requirements file. Pytest accepts unknown
markers silently, so it looked active and was not — a flaky test was reported as
a plain failure with no retry, **in CI as well as locally**. CI installs
`-r requirements.txt`, so the runner was affected too.

Proven, not inferred — a marker with `reruns=3` that needed 3 attempts:

```
ATTEMPTS = 1        # with the plugin installed this prints 3
```

## 2. The test that actually flaked

`test_overfit_small_dataset` trains a 100-step Adam run and asserts
`final_loss < 0.01`. Neither the input draw (`torch.randn`) nor the model init
was seeded. Measured over 120 unseeded runs of the same loop:

```
min=0.00046  max=0.02332  mean=0.00312
over the 0.01 threshold: 1 of 120   (0.83%)
```

That matches the one real failure observed in a full local run
(`1 failed, 6379 passed`) with nothing else in flight.

Seeded with `torch.manual_seed(0)`:

- same seed twice → byte-identical loss `0.00315112`
- seed `7` → `0.0032903`, so the seed is load-bearing, not a no-op
- 8 consecutive isolated runs pass; 17/17 in the file

**This is the underlying fix.** `reruns=2` only converted a ~1%-periodic failure
into a ~0.5% one, and until the plugin is installed the marker does nothing at
all. Seeding removes the variance instead of retrying around it.

## Not verified locally

`pip install pytest-rerunfailures` was blocked awaiting consent, so the local
venv still lacks the plugin. The requirements change is what CI reads.

2 files: `backend/requirements.txt` (+5), `backend/tests/services/test_anomaly_training.py` (+6).

issue.body:
Found by mutation while auditing `91c7c032`, not by reading the test file.

## The gap

`services/public_session_close.py` accepts a completed-session bar only if

```python
0 < bar['l'] <= min(bar['o'], bar['c']) <= max(bar['o'], bar['c']) <= bar['h']
and bar['v'] >= 0
```

`test_bad_close_fails_closed` varies **only the close**, which the ordering
constraint already rejects. The positivity and volume halves were unpinned.

Weakening `0 < bar['l']` to `-1e18 < bar['l']` left all 26 tests green:

```
# before
MUTATED: EXIT=0   26 passed
```

The new `test_implausible_bar_fields_fail_closed` — negative low, zero low,
negative volume, infinite high, NaN low — each fails for exactly one reason, and
the same mutation is now caught:

```
# after
MUTATED: EXIT=1   2 failed, 29 passed
restored: 31 passed, production file back to no diff
```

A negative low would be accepted as a real session close and flow into the spot
observation, so this is a data-integrity guard, not a formatting one.

## A correction worth keeping

The first version of this test used the **normalized short keys** (`l`, `v`) and
all 5 cases failed against *correct* production code:

```
assert 771.35 is None
```

`_extract_bars` maps the vendor's `open/high/low/close/volume` onto short keys,
so the fixture must set the long names. A test failing against correct code is a
broken test, not a discovered bug — establish which before touching production.

Production code is unchanged in this PR: `git diff --quiet
services/public_session_close.py` is clean, and ruff passes.

issue.title: docs(solstice): stop pinning a SHA that the document own merge invalidates
issue.body:
This removes a self-referential staleness loop rather than fixing one instance
of it.

`docs/solstice/STATUS.md` carried `origin/main = <sha>`. The sequence:

| PR | wrote | its own merge produced |
|---|---|---|
| #69 | `70265385` | `5dcb8774` |
| #71 | `5dcb8774` | `95173000` |

Each merge invalidated the line it had just corrected, so #71 existed **only** to
repoint a SHA. A document that names the commit its own merge creates can never
hold a correct value — repointing it is not a fix, it is the third turn of a
loop.

The counts are the durable part and each already names what moved it (6467 ->
6495 after `91c7c032`, +5 after #70, 330 -> 332 files, 103/910 -> 105/918
frontend). Those stay. The SHA line now directs the reader to
`git log -1 origin/main` and records why the pin was removed, so it does not
read as a missing value and get re-added as a regression.

Same reasoning already applies to the truth-audit count, documented one section
below: that number is a function of the checked-out commit, so the invariant
(0 failed) is stated instead of a figure.

1 file, +8/-3. No code changes.

issue.title: fix: fail closed and correct time/DST handling across 9 sites
issue.body:
## What

Stops `conviction_rank` from scoring **absent** evidence as **neutral**
confidence, and stops direction from leaking into quality.

## Why this is not the mechanism the audit described

The packet said the flow is "fuses a score once, then passes the fused score as
the flow input into rank_many, which fuses it again. Reproduced 73 -> 67.05."

The code does not do that. `flowseeker.py:2684` passes the fused blob as the
`conviction` **payload field**; it never passes a fused score as `flow`. The
real defects were three different things, all reproduced before fixing.

## The three defects

**1. Missing normalized to 0.5, not 0.0.** `_norm_conf` and `_norm_ml` returned
`0.5` for absent input while `_norm_flow` and `_norm_opp` returned `0.0`. So a
setup with no evidence at all scored:

```
ALL-MISSING conviction: 17.5 tier: LOW
components: {'flow': 0.0, 'opportunity': 0.0, 'confluence': 0.5, 'ml': 0.5}
statuses:   all four 'missing'
```

That 17.5 is entirely `0.2*0.5 + 0.15*0.5` from the two scorers holding no
data. The module's own `*_status` fields said "missing" while the component
said 0.5 — the values contradicted each other. It also outranked real-but-weak
evidence.

**2. Direction leaked into quality.** `_norm_ml` mapped DOWN→0.0 and UP→1.0,
then applied confidence around 0.5, so BULLISH at 0.8 confidence became 0.95
and the identical BEARISH mirror became 0.05. `_norm_conf` had the same shape:
`(v+100)/200` made a signed 0 read as 0.5. The docstring says the module
"never invents direction"; the arithmetic did. Measured on one full evidence
set:

| | confluence | ml | score |
|---|---|---|---|
| OLD bullish | 0.8 | 0.95 | **85.75** |
| OLD bearish | 0.2 | 0.05 | **60.25** |
| NEW either side | 0.6 | 0.45 | **74.25** |

**3. Fused blob re-read as raw input.** `rank_many` sniffed dict keys, so a
blob carrying `label` matched the ML branch and one carrying `total` matched
the confluence branch — a fused row silently gained components it never had.
An unrecognized ML label is now `unavailable`, not a silent HOLD.

## Tier change is honest, not a lowered bar

Thresholds are untouched. `test_rank_one_fuses_and_degrades` moves HIGH → MED
because the same row scores 74.25 instead of 85.75 — its inputs were being
flattered. The expectation was updated to the corrected value with the symmetry
assertion added inline. No test was skipped, xfailed, or loosened.

## Tests red before, green after

```
5 failed, 3 passed   ->   8 passed   ->   10 passed
```

## Mutations — all four killed

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| MUT1 `_norm_conf` missing → 0.5 | 2 failed |
| MUT2 `_norm_ml` missing → 0.5 | 1 failed |
| MUT3 `_norm_ml` old asymmetric map | 1 failed |
| MUT4 blob guard removed | 1 failed |

**MUT4 initially survived.** The fused `components` dict carries no
scorer-shaped keys, so no key-only assertion could distinguish it. Two tests
were added to pin the fused-marker guard specifically, after which it is killed.

## Gates

```
tests/services tests/routes: 4546 passed, 33 skipped in 244.34s
ruff check: All checks passed!
```

## Not claimed as fixed

- The route still supplies `confluence=None, ml=None` at `flowseeker.py:2614`
  and `:2684` despite the four-scorer description. Separate decision needed:
  connect causal producers, or label those dimensions unavailable.
- H2 scanner cursor/budget, H4 persistence, H5-H7 untouched by this PR.

## Standing caveat

Conviction fusion is a deterministic sort over recorded evidence. It is **not**
a calibrated win probability, and no tier here implies one. No profitability or
predictive claim is made or supported by these tests.

Refs: `.planning/INTEGRATION_H0_H7.md`



---

## Slice 2 — one availability boundary across all scorers (`b51ee581`)

The three normalizers had drifted, so `*_status` could not be trusted. Three
distinct meanings were being reported through two labels:

| payload | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| `_norm_flow({})` | 0.0 / `ok` | 0.0 / `missing` |
| `_norm_flow({"conviction": None})` | 0.0 / `invalid` | 0.0 / `missing` |
| `_norm_conf({"total": None})` | 0.0 / `invalid` | 0.0 / `missing` |
| `_norm_ml({})` | 0.0 / `invalid` | 0.0 / `missing` |
| `_norm_ml({"prediction": None})` | 0.0 / `invalid` | 0.0 / `missing` |

The confluence case is a real integration boundary, not hypothetical.
`services.agent.confluence.score` returns `{"total": None,
"direction": "insufficient_evidence"}` when it has no coverage. The producer
says "insufficient evidence"; the ranker relabelled that as "invalid" — i.e.
"this producer emitted garbage". Different operational responses, and an
unlabelled 0.0 is worse than either: indistinguishable from a measured zero.

Malformed payloads still report `invalid`; a real 0.0 still reports `ok` with a
0.0 component. "Measured and neutral" stays distinguishable from "never
measured" while both contribute nothing.

### Confirmed against live production data, not a fixture

Real call to `/api/heatseeker/node-confluence?ticker=SPY` (136 strikes
considered), feeding its actual `rows[0]["confluence"]` into `rank_one`:

```
producer total           : None
producer direction       : insufficient_evidence
ranker confluence_status : missing          <- was "invalid"
ranker component         : 0.0
conviction               : 0.0 LOW
```

### A correction I made to my own work

I initially "simplified" the empty-dict clauses in all three normalizers as
redundant. That was **wrong for confluence** — `conf.get("total", 0)` defaults
to 0, not None — and the suite caught it. Reverted, and the reason is now a
comment so the next reader does not repeat it. The `_norm_flow` clause *is*
genuinely redundant; MUT7 survived its removal, so it was deleted rather than
left as untested code.

### Mutations, slice 2

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| MUT5 `total=None` guard removed | 2 failed |
| MUT6 confluence empty-dict removed | 1 failed |
| MUT7 flow empty-dict clause restored | **survived** → clause is dead, deleted |
| MUT8 ml null-prediction guard removed | 1 failed |
| MUT9 ml empty-dict guard removed | 1 failed |

### Gates

```
local  tests/services tests/routes : 4555 passed, 33 skipped, 0 failed
CI 36414866514 (b3874cc9)           : backend 6511 passed / 0 failed
                                     frontend 918 passed, ruff pass
```

## H2 headline claim: refuted, no code changed

"Cursor advances by limit modulo the truncated length; repeated calls scan the
identical top batch" does not describe this code. `advance_cursor` rotates over
the full universe size:

```
first 3 indices per call: [(0,1,2), (10,11,12), (20,21,22), (30,31,32), (40,41,42)]
n=0 -> ([], 0)            slice>n -> ([0,1,2], 0)
```

Batches are disjoint and the degenerate cases are guarded. Recorded so it is
not re-audited as broken.

## Still not claimed fixed

- **Confluence and ML are still not wired into the route.** The producer is now
  proven *compatible* — `node_confluence` rows carry
  `{total, direction, dimensions, coverage_weight, missing_input_policy,
  weights_version}`, which `_norm_conf` consumes directly — so wiring is
  mechanical. It is deliberately not done here: it changes a live route's
  scoring behavior and deserves its own review.
- `^SPX` entitlement vs 0DTE separation; recency/invalidation; cross-batch
  leaderboard recomputation. H4–H7 untouched.

## Standing caveat

Conviction fusion is a deterministic sort over recorded evidence. It is **not**
a calibrated win probability, and no tier here implies one. Nothing in this PR
demonstrates that the strategy makes money.



---

## Slice 3 — observation age surfaced, score deliberately unchanged (`f76a5cee`)

`asof` was recorded on every row and never evaluated, so a historical alert read
as a current observation:

```
6-month-old alert : 31.5 LOW | asof 2026-03-01T00:00:00+00:00
fresh alert       : 31.5 LOW | asof 2026-09-28T00:00:00+00:00
identical score? True
```

Evidence now carries `asof_status` ∈ {fresh, stale, future, unknown,
unparseable} and `asof_age_seconds`. The 7-day window matches the alert feed
window the scan route actually reads. Absent and unparseable timestamps are
labelled, never guessed.

**The conviction score is unchanged, on purpose.** A decay curve would be a
model of how conviction decays, and there is no evidence for one here.
Applying invented decay to a fusion score is exactly the unvalidated arithmetic
this PR exists to remove. The module reports age and refuses to rescale; the
consumer decides. A test pins the diagnostic as inert with respect to
conviction.

---

## Live impact, measured on the running service

`/api/flowseeker/universe/scan` on the **pre-fix** backend (PID 46355, started
17:35, not restarted):

```
DDOG   score=23.62  tier=LOW  components={'flow': 0.175, 'opportunity': 0.0, 'confluence': 0.5, 'ml': 0.5}
OKTA   score=23.62  tier=LOW  components={'flow': 0.175, 'opportunity': 0.0, 'confluence': 0.5, 'ml': 0.5}
```

`confluence: 0.5` and `ml: 0.5` are contributed by two scorers holding **no
data at all**. The same row through the fixed module:

```
score=6.12  components={'flow': 0.175, 'opportunity': 0.0, 'confluence': 0.0, 'ml': 0.0}
statuses: flow ok, opportunity/confluence/ml missing, asof fresh
```

**23.62 → 6.12: exactly 17.5 points of phantom confidence removed from a real
production row.** The surviving 6.12 is entirely the one scorer that actually
had evidence.

Note the live backend has **not** been restarted and still runs pre-fix code;
this is a projection of the merged behaviour, not a claim about the running
service.

## Corrections made during review

1. I claimed live rows showed `conviction: 0.0`; they actually show `23.62`. My
   print was reading a nested dict incorrectly. The corrected reading is above.
2. I "simplified" all three empty-dict clauses as redundant. Wrong for
   confluence — `.get("total", 0)` defaults to 0, not None. Suite caught it.
3. MUT7 survived, revealing `_norm_flow`'s clause is genuinely dead. Deleted
   rather than left as untested code.
4. ruff flagged 3 issues on the first draft of slice 3; fixed before commit
   rather than left for CI to catch.



---

## Scope correction on `13b952bc` (the `^SPX` fix)

After committing, I checked the real universe and found the change is
**documentation-only**:

```
POPULAR_UNIVERSE size: 75
excluded count       : 0
^VIX   in POPULAR_UNIVERSE: False
^SPX   in POPULAR_UNIVERSE: False
BTC    in POPULAR_UNIVERSE: False
ETH    in POPULAR_UNIVERSE: False
```

Neither set ever intersected the shipped scan universe, so **no live scan
behavior moved** and the user-visible exposure was always zero. The
classification was still factually wrong — `^SPX` and `^VIX` have listed Cboe
options and this deployment serves `^SPX` at spot 7743.41 with 80 strike rows —
and it would have become a live exclusion the moment anyone added `^SPX` to the
universe. But it is not the defect the packet implied, and I am not claiming it
as one.

The `dte` fix (`91881cc2`) is different: `scan_batch` genuinely never forwarded
the parameter, so that one did affect every scan.



---

## Confluence / ML wiring: investigated and deliberately not done

The audit asked to "connect valid, causal, compatible producers **or** label
those dimensions unavailable." I traced the chain; the answer is the second
branch, on evidence.

**The producer is compatible.** `node_brief(ticker, strikes)` consumes the
heatmap's own `strikes` list. Verified on a live `^SPX` payload:
`structure_magnitude` → `(1.0, 'ok')`, and rows carry
`confluence = {total, direction, dimensions, coverage_weight,
missing_input_policy, weights_version}` — exactly `_norm_conf`'s input.

**But it honestly returns `total: None`.** `confluence.score` counts a
dimension only when its `inputs_status == "ok"`. `node_brief` populates only
`flow` and `microstructure`; the other four are hardcoded `0.0` with status
`"missing"`, and `structure` is `"context_only"` because it is deliberately
unsigned. No signed evidence → coverage 0.0 → `total: None`.

**And the evidence source is empty here.** Verified directly against DuckDB:

```
flow_alerts_daily  -> Catalog Error: Table ... does not exist
flow_prints        -> 0 rows
read_alert_feed()  -> 0 rows  (route's `except Exception: pass` swallows it)
```

So wiring it today would replace a truthful `None` with an equally truthful
`None`, while adding a failing query per ticker. The honest state — which this
PR now produces — is:

```
conviction: 0.0 | tier: LOW
flow_status: missing, opportunity_status: missing,
confluence_status: missing, ml_status: missing, asof_status: fresh
```

**There is no flow evidence to rank on in this deployment.** Before this PR the
same situation reported `ok` with fabricated 0.5 components and a 17.5-point
phantom score.

Deferred, not blocked: the wiring becomes worthwhile the moment `flow_prints`
is populated or a real per-strike ML producer exists. Compatibility is proven and
recorded, so it is a parameter change rather than a redesign. **Not claimed as
connected.**

---

## Scope corrections in this PR, stated plainly

1. The `^SPX` classification fix (`13b952bc`) is **documentation-only** — those
   symbols are absent from `POPULAR_UNIVERSE`, so no live behavior moved.
2. The 0DTE `dte` fix (`91881cc2`) and the leaderboard-rank fix (`c34824bf`)
   **did** affect live behavior and are the substantive route changes here.



---

## H6 — the evidence export leaked snapshot scope verbatim (`6dbe0bf3`) — SECURITY

Investigating the Muse handoff surfaced a real leak. The packet's **facts** are
a strict allowlist and were safe. The **envelope** was not:

```python
"scope": scope,      # solstice_evidence.py — verbatim copy
```

Anything the snapshot carried in `scope` left the process byte-identical.
Verified by hash rather than by eye — my display pipeline was masking the value
as `***`, which briefly made this *look* already-redacted and nearly hid it:

```
input hash  : f46033ac88af
output hash : f46033ac88af
byte-identical: True
secret present in serialized packet: True
```

Now gated by `_EXPORTABLE_SCOPE_KEYS` — an **allowlist**, so a new
credential-bearing scope key fails CLOSED instead of needing a denylist entry.
Without it, redaction held only as long as nobody added a key.

The real production scope is preserved exactly:

```
input scope : ['basis','expiries','formulaVersion','metric','signConvention']
output scope: ['basis','expiries','formulaVersion','metric','signConvention']
ALL PRESERVED: True
```

**Latent hole, not a breach that occurred** — the live packet was already clean
because production scope carries nothing sensitive. Closed before anything puts a
DSN into a snapshot scope.

New `tests/solstice/test_evidence_packet_redaction.py` (28 tests) covers the H6
edge cases against the real builder: 22 credential-shaped key names,
allowlist-not-passthrough, injected text quarantined as `UNTRUSTED_USER_TEXT`,
missing wall absent rather than zero-valued, empty snapshot not claiming
eligibility, and schema versioning. **One of these failed against the old code** —
that failure is the finding.

### Muse status: NOT connected

No documented read-only integration has been established, no local bundle
inspected, and no fallback connection prepared. The packet is the supported
fallback and is what exists. The existing packet already carries
`schema_version`, `scope.metric/basis/signConvention/formulaVersion`,

pull.title: fix: fail closed and correct time/DST handling across 9 sites
pull.body:
## What

Stops `conviction_rank` from scoring **absent** evidence as **neutral**
confidence, and stops direction from leaking into quality.

## Why this is not the mechanism the audit described

The packet said the flow is "fuses a score once, then passes the fused score as
the flow input into rank_many, which fuses it again. Reproduced 73 -> 67.05."

The code does not do that. `flowseeker.py:2684` passes the fused blob as the
`conviction` **payload field**; it never passes a fused score as `flow`. The
real defects were three different things, all reproduced before fixing.

## The three defects

**1. Missing normalized to 0.5, not 0.0.** `_norm_conf` and `_norm_ml` returned
`0.5` for absent input while `_norm_flow` and `_norm_opp` returned `0.0`. So a
setup with no evidence at all scored:

```
ALL-MISSING conviction: 17.5 tier: LOW
components: {'flow': 0.0, 'opportunity': 0.0, 'confluence': 0.5, 'ml': 0.5}
statuses:   all four 'missing'
```

That 17.5 is entirely `0.2*0.5 + 0.15*0.5` from the two scorers holding no
data. The module's own `*_status` fields said "missing" while the component
said 0.5 — the values contradicted each other. It also outranked real-but-weak
evidence.

**2. Direction leaked into quality.** `_norm_ml` mapped DOWN→0.0 and UP→1.0,
then applied confidence around 0.5, so BULLISH at 0.8 confidence became 0.95
and the identical BEARISH mirror became 0.05. `_norm_conf` had the same shape:
`(v+100)/200` made a signed 0 read as 0.5. The docstring says the module
"never invents direction"; the arithmetic did. Measured on one full evidence
set:

| | confluence | ml | score |
|---|---|---|---|
| OLD bullish | 0.8 | 0.95 | **85.75** |
| OLD bearish | 0.2 | 0.05 | **60.25** |
| NEW either side | 0.6 | 0.45 | **74.25** |

**3. Fused blob re-read as raw input.** `rank_many` sniffed dict keys, so a
blob carrying `label` matched the ML branch and one carrying `total` matched
the confluence branch — a fused row silently gained components it never had.
An unrecognized ML label is now `unavailable`, not a silent HOLD.

## Tier change is honest, not a lowered bar

Thresholds are untouched. `test_rank_one_fuses_and_degrades` moves HIGH → MED
because the same row scores 74.25 instead of 85.75 — its inputs were being
flattered. The expectation was updated to the corrected value with the symmetry
assertion added inline. No test was skipped, xfailed, or loosened.

## Tests red before, green after

```
5 failed, 3 passed   ->   8 passed   ->   10 passed
```

## Mutations — all four killed

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| MUT1 `_norm_conf` missing → 0.5 | 2 failed |
| MUT2 `_norm_ml` missing → 0.5 | 1 failed |
| MUT3 `_norm_ml` old asymmetric map | 1 failed |
| MUT4 blob guard removed | 1 failed |

**MUT4 initially survived.** The fused `components` dict carries no
scorer-shaped keys, so no key-only assertion could distinguish it. Two tests
were added to pin the fused-marker guard specifically, after which it is killed.

## Gates

```
tests/services tests/routes: 4546 passed, 33 skipped in 244.34s
ruff check: All checks passed!
```

## Not claimed as fixed

- The route still supplies `confluence=None, ml=None` at `flowseeker.py:2614`
  and `:2684` despite the four-scorer description. Separate decision needed:
  connect causal producers, or label those dimensions unavailable.
- H2 scanner cursor/budget, H4 persistence, H5-H7 untouched by this PR.

## Standing caveat

Conviction fusion is a deterministic sort over recorded evidence. It is **not**
a calibrated win probability, and no tier here implies one. No profitability or
predictive claim is made or supported by these tests.

Refs: `.planning/INTEGRATION_H0_H7.md`



---

## Slice 2 — one availability boundary across all scorers (`b51ee581`)

The three normalizers had drifted, so `*_status` could not be trusted. Three
distinct meanings were being reported through two labels:

| payload | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| `_norm_flow({})` | 0.0 / `ok` | 0.0 / `missing` |
| `_norm_flow({"conviction": None})` | 0.0 / `invalid` | 0.0 / `missing` |
| `_norm_conf({"total": None})` | 0.0 / `invalid` | 0.0 / `missing` |
| `_norm_ml({})` | 0.0 / `invalid` | 0.0 / `missing` |
| `_norm_ml({"prediction": None})` | 0.0 / `invalid` | 0.0 / `missing` |

The confluence case is a real integration boundary, not hypothetical.
`services.agent.confluence.score` returns `{"total": None,
"direction": "insufficient_evidence"}` when it has no coverage. The producer
says "insufficient evidence"; the ranker relabelled that as "invalid" — i.e.
"this producer emitted garbage". Different operational responses, and an
unlabelled 0.0 is worse than either: indistinguishable from a measured zero.

Malformed payloads still report `invalid`; a real 0.0 still reports `ok` with a
0.0 component. "Measured and neutral" stays distinguishable from "never
measured" while both contribute nothing.

### Confirmed against live production data, not a fixture

Real call to `/api/heatseeker/node-confluence?ticker=SPY` (136 strikes
considered), feeding its actual `rows[0]["confluence"]` into `rank_one`:

```
producer total           : None
producer direction       : insufficient_evidence
ranker confluence_status : missing          <- was "invalid"
ranker component         : 0.0
conviction               : 0.0 LOW
```

### A correction I made to my own work

I initially "simplified" the empty-dict clauses in all three normalizers as
redundant. That was **wrong for confluence** — `conf.get("total", 0)` defaults
to 0, not None — and the suite caught it. Reverted, and the reason is now a
comment so the next reader does not repeat it. The `_norm_flow` clause *is*
genuinely redundant; MUT7 survived its removal, so it was deleted rather than
left as untested code.

### Mutations, slice 2

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| MUT5 `total=None` guard removed | 2 failed |
| MUT6 confluence empty-dict removed | 1 failed |
| MUT7 flow empty-dict clause restored | **survived** → clause is dead, deleted |
| MUT8 ml null-prediction guard removed | 1 failed |
| MUT9 ml empty-dict guard removed | 1 failed |

### Gates

```
local  tests/services tests/routes : 4555 passed, 33 skipped, 0 failed
CI 36414866514 (b3874cc9)           : backend 6511 passed / 0 failed
                                     frontend 918 passed, ruff pass
```

## H2 headline claim: refuted, no code changed

"Cursor advances by limit modulo the truncated length; repeated calls scan the
identical top batch" does not describe this code. `advance_cursor` rotates over
the full universe size:

```
first 3 indices per call: [(0,1,2), (10,11,12), (20,21,22), (30,31,32), (40,41,42)]
n=0 -> ([], 0)            slice>n -> ([0,1,2], 0)
```

Batches are disjoint and the degenerate cases are guarded. Recorded so it is
not re-audited as broken.

## Still not claimed fixed

- **Confluence and ML are still not wired into the route.** The producer is now
  proven *compatible* — `node_confluence` rows carry
  `{total, direction, dimensions, coverage_weight, missing_input_policy,
  weights_version}`, which `_norm_conf` consumes directly — so wiring is
  mechanical. It is deliberately not done here: it changes a live route's
  scoring behavior and deserves its own review.
- `^SPX` entitlement vs 0DTE separation; recency/invalidation; cross-batch
  leaderboard recomputation. H4–H7 untouched.

## Standing caveat

Conviction fusion is a deterministic sort over recorded evidence. It is **not**
a calibrated win probability, and no tier here implies one. Nothing in this PR
demonstrates that the strategy makes money.



---

## Slice 3 — observation age surfaced, score deliberately unchanged (`f76a5cee`)

`asof` was recorded on every row and never evaluated, so a historical alert read
as a current observation:

```
6-month-old alert : 31.5 LOW | asof 2026-03-01T00:00:00+00:00
fresh alert       : 31.5 LOW | asof 2026-09-28T00:00:00+00:00
identical score? True
```

Evidence now carries `asof_status` ∈ {fresh, stale, future, unknown,
unparseable} and `asof_age_seconds`. The 7-day window matches the alert feed
window the scan route actually reads. Absent and unparseable timestamps are
labelled, never guessed.

**The conviction score is unchanged, on purpose.** A decay curve would be a
model of how conviction decays, and there is no evidence for one here.
Applying invented decay to a fusion score is exactly the unvalidated arithmetic
this PR exists to remove. The module reports age and refuses to rescale; the
consumer decides. A test pins the diagnostic as inert with respect to
conviction.

---

## Live impact, measured on the running service

`/api/flowseeker/universe/scan` on the **pre-fix** backend (PID 46355, started
17:35, not restarted):

```
DDOG   score=23.62  tier=LOW  components={'flow': 0.175, 'opportunity': 0.0, 'confluence': 0.5, 'ml': 0.5}
OKTA   score=23.62  tier=LOW  components={'flow': 0.175, 'opportunity': 0.0, 'confluence': 0.5, 'ml': 0.5}
```

`confluence: 0.5` and `ml: 0.5` are contributed by two scorers holding **no
data at all**. The same row through the fixed module:

```
score=6.12  components={'flow': 0.175, 'opportunity': 0.0, 'confluence': 0.0, 'ml': 0.0}
statuses: flow ok, opportunity/confluence/ml missing, asof fresh
```

**23.62 → 6.12: exactly 17.5 points of phantom confidence removed from a real
production row.** The surviving 6.12 is entirely the one scorer that actually
had evidence.

Note the live backend has **not** been restarted and still runs pre-fix code;
this is a projection of the merged behaviour, not a claim about the running
service.

## Corrections made during review

1. I claimed live rows showed `conviction: 0.0`; they actually show `23.62`. My
   print was reading a nested dict incorrectly. The corrected reading is above.
2. I "simplified" all three empty-dict clauses as redundant. Wrong for
   confluence — `.get("total", 0)` defaults to 0, not None. Suite caught it.
3. MUT7 survived, revealing `_norm_flow`'s clause is genuinely dead. Deleted
   rather than left as untested code.
4. ruff flagged 3 issues on the first draft of slice 3; fixed before commit
   rather than left for CI to catch.



---

## Scope correction on `13b952bc` (the `^SPX` fix)

After committing, I checked the real universe and found the change is
**documentation-only**:

```
POPULAR_UNIVERSE size: 75
excluded count       : 0
^VIX   in POPULAR_UNIVERSE: False
^SPX   in POPULAR_UNIVERSE: False
BTC    in POPULAR_UNIVERSE: False
ETH    in POPULAR_UNIVERSE: False
```

Neither set ever intersected the shipped scan universe, so **no live scan
behavior moved** and the user-visible exposure was always zero. The
classification was still factually wrong — `^SPX` and `^VIX` have listed Cboe
options and this deployment serves `^SPX` at spot 7743.41 with 80 strike rows —
and it would have become a live exclusion the moment anyone added `^SPX` to the
universe. But it is not the defect the packet implied, and I am not claiming it
as one.

The `dte` fix (`91881cc2`) is different: `scan_batch` genuinely never forwarded
the parameter, so that one did affect every scan.



---

## Confluence / ML wiring: investigated and deliberately not done

The audit asked to "connect valid, causal, compatible producers **or** label
those dimensions unavailable." I traced the chain; the answer is the second
branch, on evidence.

**The producer is compatible.** `node_brief(ticker, strikes)` consumes the
heatmap's own `strikes` list. Verified on a live `^SPX` payload:
`structure_magnitude` → `(1.0, 'ok')`, and rows carry
`confluence = {total, direction, dimensions, coverage_weight,
missing_input_policy, weights_version}` — exactly `_norm_conf`'s input.

**But it honestly returns `total: None`.** `confluence.score` counts a
dimension only when its `inputs_status == "ok"`. `node_brief` populates only
`flow` and `microstructure`; the other four are hardcoded `0.0` with status
`"missing"`, and `structure` is `"context_only"` because it is deliberately
unsigned. No signed evidence → coverage 0.0 → `total: None`.

**And the evidence source is empty here.** Verified directly against DuckDB:

```
flow_alerts_daily  -> Catalog Error: Table ... does not exist
flow_prints        -> 0 rows
read_alert_feed()  -> 0 rows  (route's `except Exception: pass` swallows it)
```

So wiring it today would replace a truthful `None` with an equally truthful
`None`, while adding a failing query per ticker. The honest state — which this
PR now produces — is:

```
conviction: 0.0 | tier: LOW
flow_status: missing, opportunity_status: missing,
confluence_status: missing, ml_status: missing, asof_status: fresh
```

**There is no flow evidence to rank on in this deployment.** Before this PR the
same situation reported `ok` with fabricated 0.5 components and a 17.5-point
phantom score.

Deferred, not blocked: the wiring becomes worthwhile the moment `flow_prints`
is populated or a real per-strike ML producer exists. Compatibility is proven and
recorded, so it is a parameter change rather than a redesign. **Not claimed as
connected.**

---

## Scope corrections in this PR, stated plainly

1. The `^SPX` classification fix (`13b952bc`) is **documentation-only** — those
   symbols are absent from `POPULAR_UNIVERSE`, so no live behavior moved.
2. The 0DTE `dte` fix (`91881cc2`) and the leaderboard-rank fix (`c34824bf`)
   **did** affect live behavior and are the substantive route changes here.



---

## H6 — the evidence export leaked snapshot scope verbatim (`6dbe0bf3`) — SECURITY

Investigating the Muse handoff surfaced a real leak. The packet's **facts** are
a strict allowlist and were safe. The **envelope** was not:

```python
"scope": scope,      # solstice_evidence.py — verbatim copy
```

Anything the snapshot carried in `scope` left the process byte-identical.
Verified by hash rather than by eye — my display pipeline was masking the value
as `***`, which briefly made this *look* already-redacted and nearly hid it:

```
input hash  : f46033ac88af
output hash : f46033ac88af
byte-identical: True
secret present in serialized packet: True
```

Now gated by `_EXPORTABLE_SCOPE_KEYS` — an **allowlist**, so a new
credential-bearing scope key fails CLOSED instead of needing a denylist entry.
Without it, redaction held only as long as nobody added a key.

The real production scope is preserved exactly:

```
input scope : ['basis','expiries','formulaVersion','metric','signConvention']
output scope: ['basis','expiries','formulaVersion','metric','signConvention']
ALL PRESERVED: True
```

**Latent hole, not a breach that occurred** — the live packet was already clean
because production scope carries nothing sensitive. Closed before anything puts a
DSN into a snapshot scope.

New `tests/solstice/test_evidence_packet_redaction.py` (28 tests) covers the H6
edge cases against the real builder: 22 credential-shaped key names,
allowlist-not-passthrough, injected text quarantined as `UNTRUSTED_USER_TEXT`,
missing wall absent rather than zero-valued, empty snapshot not claiming
eligibility, and schema versioning. **One of these failed against the old code** —
that failure is the finding.

### Muse status: NOT connected

No documented read-only integration has been established, no local bundle
inspected, and no fallback connection prepared. The packet is the supported
fallback and is what exists. The existing packet already carries
`schema_version`, `scope.metric/basis/signConvention/formulaVersion`,
`quality.setupEligible` + `reasonCodes`, and
`environment.inventory_basis = CONVENTIONAL_PROXY` — an honest label that the
service does not know real dealer inventory. Recording the limitation rather than
pretending it is connected.

issue.title: fix(truth-audit): match the subject line, not the whole commit message
issue.body:
Fixes the gate that blocked the #73 merge.

## The failure

The #73 merge commit (`433d99ab`) failed CI:

```
FAIL: Refactor commit: server.py must not grow (currently 4047 lines, baseline 3532)
```

The trigger was the word `refactor` appearing **once in the commit body**, in a
sentence explaining why the evidence-packet leak mattered. `server.py` was
already 4047 lines from earlier work that this commit never touched:

```
git diff --name-only 29f74d8a..a65f6a3a | grep -c server.py   -> 0
git show d905c9d2:backend/server.py | wc -l                    -> 4047
git show 29f74d8a:backend/server.py | wc -l                    -> 4047
```

A correct merge was blocked by a word in a sentence. `server.py` is frozen for
the integration lane, so the fix belongs in the gate, not the file.

## Root cause

Rules 1 and 2 gate on what a commit **claims to do**, so they must read the
subject line. They matched the entire message instead, making a commit
*describing* work indistinguishable from one *declaring* it.

The script already knew this. Its own comments record that Rules 9-12 hit the
identical problem and were scoped to the subject — *"this very rule blocked its
own commit that way on the first try."* Rules 1 and 2 were never brought in
line. `COMMIT_SUBJECT` is now defined once, above Rule 1; the duplicate
definition further down is removed.

## The rule is not neutered

Verified in both directions:

- Current tree: **227 passed, 0 failed**
- A synthetic commit whose **subject** is `refactor: reorganize backend` still
  fails Rule 2 (**226 passed, 1 failed**)

A real refactor claim is still caught, which is the point of the rule.

Also: the `Message:` banner previously echoed `git log` while the rules read a
separately-derived first line, so the audit could print something it had not
actually evaluated. One variable now feeds both.

issue.title: fix(alerts): a boolean was broadcast as a bearish momentum alert
issue.body:
A boolean could be broadcast to every `/ws/signals` client as a bearish
momentum alert.

## The bug

`_parse_momentum_score` coerced with `int(float(raw))`. Since `bool` subclasses
`int`, `float(True)` is `1.0` — so a boolean became a real score of **1**:

```
MOMENTUM_EXTREME_HIGH = 80      # score > 80 -> extreme bullish
MOMENTUM_EXTREME_LOW  = 20      # score < 20 -> extreme bearish
```

Measured before the fix:

| input | parsed | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `True` | 1 | **BEARISH ALERT** |
| `False` | 0 | **BEARISH ALERT** |
| `85` | 85 | BULLISH ALERT |
| `10` | 10 | BEARISH ALERT |

This is the live signal path: the resulting alert goes to `broadcast_signal`
and reaches every connected `/ws/signals` client, so a value that was never a
measurement could appear in the UI as *"Strong BEARISH momentum — score 1/100"*.

Booleans are now rejected like any other malformed input.

## The 50 fallback, and why it stays

It is a **no-alert sentinel, not a measurement** — 50 sits inside the dead band
(20..80), so unavailable momentum cannot fire an alert. That was luck rather
than design, so it is now asserted: if the thresholds move, absent data starts
broadcasting alerts and these tests fail.

A real reading of 50 and unavailable data still return the same value.
Distinguishing them properly means returning a status alongside the score, which
is a wider change to the detector contract than this fix should make on its own.

## Tests

2 added to `tests/routes/test_alert_plumbing.py`. One failed against the old
code with `bool True must not become a score, got 1`.

- `test_booleans_are_not_momentum_scores`
- `test_missing_and_malformed_are_not_measured_neutral_readings`

MUT26 (bool guard removed) → 1 failed.

## Sibling sweep

The other 13 broad-`except` sites in `routes/` were checked for the same shape.
They are correct — each leaves the key **absent** rather than fabricating a
value, with the degradation documented inline (`steal_three.py:224`,
`ml_api.py:554` paper metrics; `analytics.py:372` cache). `alerts.py:59` was
already correct for the same reason.

## Gates

`tests/routes` 346 passed; ruff clean.

issue.title: fix(observability): the health endpoint 500'd during exactly the outages it exists to report
issue.body:
Three fixes, all found by verifying behavior rather than trusting green tests.

## 1. The health endpoint 500'd during exactly the outages it exists to report

Found by probing the running server — the test suite was green throughout.

```
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' localhost:8000/api/data/health
500
```

`ProviderStats.seconds_since_last_success` returned `float("inf")` when a
provider had never succeeded. That propagated into the `provider_down` alert
dict, and `inf` is not JSON compliant, so response encoding raised
`ValueError`.

The route's own `except Exception` could not catch it — **serialization happens
after the handler returns, outside the try block.** So a provider that had never
succeeded took the health endpoint down with it. The 200 was only reachable
because no provider had been recorded yet.

Fixed to `None`. Alerting semantics preserved deliberately: a never-succeeded
provider is a *stronger* statement than "more than N seconds ago", so it still
fires `provider_down`:

```python
is_down = since is None or since > self.provider_down_seconds
```

The Prometheus gauge cannot hold `None`, and `0` would read as "just
succeeded" — the opposite of the truth — so the gauge uses `+inf`, which a
Gauge *can* hold.

Same class in the vol models: `rmse = inf` across 9 sites in
`SABRModel.fit` / `SVIProfile.fit`. Reachable through the
`POST /api/vol-surface/{t}/sabr` guard, since negative/NaN vols are filtered
*internally* after the `len >= 4` check. Behind auth, so latent rather than
live — I verified that before spending time on it.

## 2. A test making 75 real calls to api.public.com

`test_total_provider_failure_is_unavailable_then_stale` called `get_movers()`
**unconditionally**, and guarded only its *assertions*:

```python
stale = asyncio.run(movers_svc.get_movers(limit=5))   # always ran
live = movers_svc.completed_session_pair(now=datetime.now(UTC))
if live == (last, prior):                             # only this was guarded
```

`get_movers` fans out over the full 75-ticker universe. On any day the pair
differed, the test still made 75 outbound requests and discarded the response.

Caught by the session-scoped guard in `tests/offline_network.py`, which
correctly fails closed — but it asserts at *teardown*, so the failure surfaced
against whichever test ran last and pointed at the wrong file entirely. That's
why it appeared as an unrelated error in `test_wall_restore_latest.py`.

```
before: 651 passed, 1 error in 18.40s
after:  651 passed, 0 error in  8.85s
```

The ~10s drop is the 75 blocked network attempts no longer made.

## 3. `_reset_state` left the shared budget poisoned

`test_upstream_seam_calls_real_adapter_signature_and_shape` failed in CI with
`Expected mock to have been awaited once. Awaited 0 times`, and passed in
isolation — which is what made it look order-random.

`public_budget.budget` is a module-level singleton whose state outlives a
test. `market_bars._reset_state()` cleared the bar cache, quarantine counter
and last-error field, but **not the budget**. With a cooldown still active,
`_get` returned early at the budget gate and never reached the broker.

```
before: RESULT bars: None       RESULT awaited: 0
after:  RESULT bars: [...1 bar] RESULT awaited: 1
```

Draining tokens was not enough — the budget refills. It is specifically the
cooldown that reproduces this.

## Tests

| suite | result |
|---|---|
| `tests/routes` + `tests/solstice` | 651 passed |
| `tests/services` + `test_r7_1_red` | 4245 passed, 33 skipped |
| `tests/services/test_market_bars_reset_state.py` | 3 passed |
| `tests/test_movers_route.py` | 2 passed |

Mutations, all killed: MUT27 `seconds_since_last_success` → inf (5 failed),
MUT28 `is_down` ignores None (2 failed), MUT29 rmse → inf (2 failed),
MUT30 budget reset removed (3 failed).

The new budget tests drive the real seam through a mocked broker, so they
exercise the actual budget gate rather than asserting on the reset helper.

issue.title: test(movers): fix a fixture that failed ~70% of calendar days
issue.body:
test(movers): fix a fixture that failed ~70% of calendar days

test_movers_v2_contract_ranked_and_limited fails on every weekday and passes
on weekends. Pre-existing, confirmed on pristine origin/main with none of my
changes applied.

    $ git checkout origin/main && pytest tests/test_movers_route.py
    FAILED test_movers_v2_contract_ranked_and_limited - assert 0 == 2

Cause: the fixture built bars by walking back 10 CALENDAR days from now and
stopping at yesterday:

    for back in range(10, 0, -1):
        day = (datetime.now(UTC) - timedelta(days=back)).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")

But services.movers.get_movers reads the last two COMPLETED exchange sessions,
and on any weekday the most recent one is TODAY. The fixture could never cover
it, so the route correctly returned no rows:

    status: unavailable
    coverage: {'requested': 75, 'valid': 0, 'excluded': 75}
    session_date: 2026-09-28  prior: 2026-09-25
    fixture days: 2026-09-18 -> 2026-09-27   (today missing)

This is a TEST bug, not a production defect. The route behaved correctly -- it
reports the sessions it asked for and excludes what it did not get, and
`status: unavailable` is the honest answer rather than an empty list dressed up
as "no movers".

The fixture now takes its dates from the service's own
`completed_session_pair()`, so it is correct on any calendar day. Drift is
applied across the emitted bars in order, so the expected ranking is unchanged.

Verified calendar-independent rather than just green today, by sampling the
pair over 200 hypothetical dates spanning +/-400 days:

    new fixture: 0 of 200 missing the session pair
    old fixture: 141 of 200 missing the session pair  (~70%)

Tests: tests/test_movers_route.py 2 passed.

issue.title: fix(eastern-clock): US DST rule for all four ET gates (rebased on #84)
issue.body:
fix(eastern-clock): US DST rule for all four ET gates, rebased on #84

The host-tm_isdst fallback existed in four places, each gating something
that matters:

  server._in_window_now_et      the 09:00-10:30 ET live window
  server._scheduler_loop        OI prefetch gate
  server.flow_sse               the trading-window gate on real streaming
  alert_dispatcher._is_quiet_hours   whether an outbound call is suppressed

`time.localtime().tm_isdst` reports the HOST timezone, not Eastern's. US and
EU DST begin and end on different dates, so for roughly Mar 8-28 and Oct 25-31
each year the host's answer is wrong about Eastern's. A one-hour error opens
or closes a window at the wrong time, and on the quiet-hours gate it lands
directly on the 22:00/21:59 boundary.

The arithmetic now lives in services/eastern_clock.py and applies the US rule
directly (second Sunday in March 07:00 UTC -> first Sunday in November
06:00 UTC), needing no tz database and correct wherever the host runs.
`grep tm_isdst` over production code returns one hit: a docstring saying why.

_in_window_now_et now fails closed if even the arithmetic fallback raises.

19 tests across three files, each driving the real function with zoneinfo
forced to fail and time.localtime reporting a foreign host's DST flag.
MUT30/31/32 all killed.

Local: 6639 passed, 37 skipped, 1 error. The single error is a PRE-EXISTING
credential-gated network leak owned by Command Code (b1f06d18) and is
documented in .planning/INTEGRATION_H0_H7.md rather than patched here, since
services/agentfield_hub.py is their ownership lane. It reproduces on this
checkout only because backend/.env holds a real PUBLIC_API_KEY; CI has no key
and cannot see it. The suite is green with that file absent.

Rebased onto 53d8237a (PR #84). Zero file overlap with it; the server.py
conflict was context drift, and the resolved diff touches only the ET lines.
Supersedes the earlier head on #85.

The host-tm_isdst fallback existed in four places, each gating something
that matters:

  server._in_window_now_et      the 09:00-10:30 ET live window
  server._scheduler_loop        OI prefetch gate
  server.flow_sse               the trading-window gate on real streaming
  alert_dispatcher._is_quiet_hours   whether an outbound call is suppressed

`time.localtime().tm_isdst` reports the HOST timezone, not Eastern's. US and
EU DST begin and end on different dates, so for roughly Mar 8-28 and Oct 25-31
each year the host's answer is wrong about Eastern's. A one-hour error opens
or closes a window at the wrong time, and on the quiet-hours gate it lands
directly on the 22:00/21:59 boundary.

The arithmetic now lives in services/eastern_clock.py and applies the US rule
directly (second Sunday in March 07:00 UTC -> first Sunday in November
06:00 UTC), needing no tz database and correct wherever the host runs.
`grep tm_isdst` over production code returns one hit: a docstring saying why.

_in_window_now_et now fails closed if even the arithmetic fallback raises.

19 tests across three files, each driving the real function with zoneinfo
forced to fail and time.localtime reporting a foreign host's DST flag.
